name: DPM++ 2M
plain: Second-order multistep DPM++ on x0 in −log σ: reuse the previous x0 prediction to correct the current step for one call per step. Deterministic, and the step formula has no special flow-model handling.
math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
t=−log σ, h=t'−t, r=h_last/h, D̄=(1+1/(2r))D−(1/(2r))D_old.
x'=(σ'/σ)x−(e^{−h}−1)D̄. First step and σ'=0 step use D̄=D.

props.final_sigma0: σ'=0 uses the first-order branch; t'=inf gives e^{−h}=0 and σ_fn(t')=0, so x'=D through IEEE inf with no separate return.
props.flow_const: No CONST branch. Uses −log σ, not logit, even on flow models; first-order form is the Euler line. Compare 2M SDE which does switch to logit.

label: from code
surprise: dpmpp_2m and dpmpp_2m_sde step in different time variables on flow models: −log σ here, logit-based half-logSNR there. At η=0 on CONST the first-order part coincides algebraically but the second-order term differs.
